name: movfuscator
listed_description: The single instruction C compiler, compiling programs into only mov instructions.
reason: Opened the README and repo page (10.6k stars, folders movfuscator, overview, poc, post, slides, softfloat, validation): no timings and no comparison against GCC or any other compiler. The only speed statement is that --no-mov-flow (jmp for control flow) 'will substantially speed up execution in larger projects' relative to its own default, with no number. The project is an obfuscation proof of concept, not a speed claim.

name: Open Watcom
listed_description: Watcom C, C++, and Fortran cross compilers and tools.
reason: Opened the org page, open-watcom-v2 repo page and README, the open-watcom-v2-wikidocs docs listing (compiler guides, library references, no benchmark page), and FrenkelS/djdoom (a Doom DOS compiler shootout of DJGPP, Digital Mars, CC386 and Watcom whose README gives no results); also FastDoom and Doom8088 READMEs. No numeric comparison against any baseline was found. A search snippet (page not opened) says Open Watcom 1.1 compiled slower than GCC 3.2 (6578 ms release vs 2031 ms), which is the wrong direction anyway.

name: Oracle Solaris Studio
listed_description: C, C++ and Fortran compiler for SPARC and x86. Supports C++11. Available on Linux and Solaris.
reason: No page with numbers could be opened: oracle.com returned HTTP 403, and arxiv.org, phoronix.com, lists.opencsw.org, uva.es, docs.oracle.com and research.spec.org were blocked by the egress proxy. Search snippets only (not recordable) point to Sun Studio 12 vs GCC 4.1.2/4.3.2 SPEC CPU2006 comparisons from Universidad de Valladolid, a Phoronix forum thread 'Sun Studio 12 vs GCC3 vs GCC4 Benchmarks', an OpenCSW maintainers list thread 'Solaris Studio vs GCC' (March 2012), and an arXiv SPARC study where Sun C 5.11 (-m64 -fast -native) was reported 33% better than GCC 4.5.1 on arithmetic operations (arXiv 1106.2992 or 1308.6469, unclear which). Retry from an environment that can reach those hosts.

name: PCC
listed_description: A very old C compiler. Supports C99.
reason: Opened the repo page and README: a CVS-snapshot mirror (pcc-cvs-20180920) whose README only describes provenance and the BSD licence, no speed claims. pcc.ludd.ltu.se and the NetBSD mail archive are blocked. A search snippet (not opened) says PCC output was almost 50% slower than GCC on a 2001 VAX test, and Phoronix tried to benchmark PCC but most C tests failed to build, so no faster-than-baseline number exists on a reachable page.
